paper.title: Real-time machine learning model to predict in-hospital cardiac arrest using heart rate variability in ICU
paper.claim: The paper uses 33 selected HRV measures from five-minute ICU ECG epochs to predict an in-hospital cardiac-arrest event within 0.5 to 24 hours.
paper.population: Single-center retrospective cohort of 4821 critically ill patients across 5679 ICU stays at Seoul National University Hospital; it is not a home-wearable or Brainstem validation population.
paper.referenceStandard: The first documented cardiopulmonary-resuscitation event and its time during an ICU stay, linked to preceding continuous ECG epochs.
paper.relationEvidence: The CC-BY paper's code-availability statement links the audited repository. The repository has no software license and contains an incomplete training script rather than a distributable inference package.

labels: no cardiac arrest within 0.5 to 24 hours

sources.name: CC-BY paper method in Europe PMC XML

compatibility.brainstemContract: not-defined: proposed continuous ICU ECG and cardiac-event contract
requiredSignals: continuous ECG or beat-to-beat intervals sufficient for the exact 33 selected HRV measures
ICU stay context with adjudicated cardiac-arrest event and timing
compatibility.window: Five-minute epochs sampled throughout 0.5 to 24 hours before the first in-hospital cardiac-arrest event or a matched control period.
compatibility.preprocessing: Withheld until a licensed implementation and data freeze the paper's ECG quality screen, NeuroKit2 feature settings, selected-feature order, missingness, fitted model, calibration, and uncertainty.
mismatches: Brainstem home recordings are not continuous ICU telemetry.
Brainstem has no adjudicated in-hospital cardiac-arrest event or event-time reference standard.
The paper population is critically ill ICU patients from one hospital.
The linked source has no license, data, selected-feature manifest, fitted model, or saved hyperparameters.
The linked training script references undefined optimization code and cannot reproduce the paper as committed.

cohort.output: Withheld; the current Brainstem cohort does not match the paper's ICU population, telemetry, or outcome contract.
